title: Machine learning screening identifies an efficient molecular photocatalytic CO2-reduction system
summary: A machine-learning-accelerated descriptor workflow screened 3,444 molecular photosensitizer–catalyst systems, including 180,000 conformations, and selected six candidates for experimental validation. The primary article reports that the optimal tested system reached a turnover number of 4,390 and uses time-resolved spectroscopy and first-principles calculations to examine dipole coupling. The reported outcome is bounded to the tested system and the study’s screening scope.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening using descriptors for photosensitization, electron transfer, and catalysis
organization: University of Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: The article reports experimental validation of the machine-learning-screened molecular photocatalytic systems; its optimal system achieved a turnover number of 4,390. The study screened 3,444 systems and selected six promising candidates.
evidence.unknown: The summary does not identify a catalyst or photosensitizer structure because the accessible primary indexed passage did not unambiguously tie a named complex to the reported maximum. Performance is specific to the reported experimental conditions; deployment and independent replication are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning accelerates high-throughput screening with descriptors spanning photosensitization, electron transfer and catalysis, reducing the 3,444-system search to six candidates selected for experimental validation.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Catalysis indexed article text, abstract, extended-data descriptions, metadata and affiliation block; institutional research announcement checked as corroboration.
